builds.name: Reference: Ranked top core
builds.goal: Reference for Kennen: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ top players use most (2,638 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 52.8% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A ranged skirmisher who accumulates storm marks, then uses speed to deliver an area stun ultimate. The current top provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Hextech Rocketbelt → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass. Electrocute keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Sorcerer's Shoes, Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff.
builds.summary: The proven top baseline: Hextech Rocketbelt → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass, with Electrocute.
testPlan: Play it in top as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Hextech Rocketbelt → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 52.8% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Hextech Rocketbelt → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

builds.name: Lightning Rush crit extension
builds.summary: Keep the post-Rush attack-speed window alive through real crits.
builds.goal: Keep the post-Rush attack-speed window alive through real crits.
builds.hypothesis: Lightning Rush grants 50-90% attack speed for four seconds after ending, and current primary text says critical strikes extend it one second. Yun Tal builds crit through attacks, Infinity Edge supports actual crit damage, and Stormrazor helps kite while W's every-fifth attack adds magic damage with AP/AD terms. Terminus addresses the mixed ordinary attack and W output.
testPlan: Required state: Need E ended, actual crit attacks landing and W counter tracked.
Measure extension duration, crit count and fifth-W damage versus an enemy that disengages.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: No attack access means the window expires; AD investment weakens Q/R burst and mobility consumes energy.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Extension is conditional on crit events; E itself does not crit or grant permanent attack speed.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Yun Tal Wildarrows, Infinity Edge, Stormrazor, Terminus, Bloodthirster, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Survive without mana spending
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Kennen: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A ranged skirmisher who accumulates storm marks, then uses speed to deliver an area stun ultimate. Compare mark-based stun and R contact with a real W/passive attack experiment. Energy, mark cooldowns and getting into ult range prevent unlimited spell/attack procs. Stasis, a spell shield and movement may preserve repeat casts without wasting an item on mana.
builds.summary: Stasis, a spell shield and movement may preserve repeat casts without wasting an item on mana.
testPlan: Kit question for Kennen: Compare mark-based stun and R contact with a real W/passive attack experiment. Energy, mark cooldowns and getting into ult range prevent unlimited spell/attack procs.

Start with the early core (Zhonya or Banshee according to the threat, then Cosmic) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Resource: Energy. Do not treat mana regeneration as Energy recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Stasis, a spell shield and movement may preserve repeat casts without wasting an item on mana. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Kennen throws a fast moving shuriken towards a location, causing damage and adding a Mark of the Storm to any opponent that it hits. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; protection must answer an actual threat.

The route fails Kennen's stated kit question: Compare mark-based stun and R contact with a real W/passive attack experiment. Energy, mark cooldowns and getting into ult range prevent unlimited spell/attack procs.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; protection must answer an actual threat.
Full cost 16,100 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Zhonya or Banshee according to the threat, then Cosmic. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Rylai's Crystal Scepter, Cosmic Drive, Void Staff are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Resource: Energy. Do not treat mana regeneration as Energy recovery; Nimbus replaces Manaflow when that Sorcery row is used.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Storm resistance shred dive
builds.summary: Use repeated storm hits to develop shred while surviving the stun cycle.
builds.goal: Use repeated storm hits to develop shred while surviving the stun cycle.
builds.hypothesis: Slicing Maelstrom hits every 0.5 seconds for three seconds, gains damage on successive hits and grants armor/MR. Bloodletter can shred MR through qualifying ability hits; Riftmaker needs sustained combat and Rocketbelt helps maintain storm contact. Zhonya's is a survival tool after committing, while passive marks require three stacks for a stun and energy return.
testPlan: Required state: Need an entry angle, enemy escape constrained and passive marks developing on priority targets.
Track storm hit count, shred stacks and stun timing against two separated moving targets.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Blink escapes or early interruption limits storm hits; holding Zhonya too long risks dying first.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Six ticks are not guaranteed on every target and repeated marks have their own stun behavior.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Hextech Rocketbelt, Bloodletter's Curse, Riftmaker, Zhonya's Hourglass, Rabadon's Deathcap, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
